# DAT

> Distributed Access Token - a token specification where expiry, an encrypted region and key
> rotation are part of the wire format rather than optional extras, with clients for many languages
> that all speak the same protocol.

A DAT is one ASCII string of five dot-separated fields - `expire.cid.plain.secure.signature` - read
by slicing at the delimiters, with **no JSON parsing anywhere**. Every token carries an expiration
time because the format has nowhere to omit it. Sensitive data goes in a `secure` region that is
AES-GCM encrypted by construction, so there is no separate encryption spec to bolt on. The
certificate that signs a token also carries the window during which it may issue, so key rolling
happens on a schedule instead of whenever an operator remembers. The token names no algorithm at
all - the certificate decides - which removes the `alg`-confusion attack surface that JWT has.
Clients exist for Rust, Java/Kotlin, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, C#, Go, Ruby and C/C++; a token
issued by any of them verifies in all the others.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://dat.saro.me/llms/overview.md): What DAT is, the manager/certificate/token model, cluster roles, plain vs secure, client list
- [Token format](https://dat.saro.me/llms/token.md): The five fields, canonical parsing rules, issuance and verification steps
- [Certificate](https://dat.saro.me/llms/certificate.md): Certificate fields, issuance window and lifecycle, algorithms, verify-only export, rotation
- [CMS sync](https://dat.saro.me/llms/cms-sync.md): `DatCmsManager` configuration, the sync protocol, why startup never fails on a sync error, why verifyOnly stays off unless asked
- [Error codes](https://dat.saro.me/llms/errors.md): Every `DAT_*` code with retry class and impact, plus a symptom index
- [Integration patterns](https://dat.saro.me/llms/integration.md): Issuing and verifying tiers, payload design, refresh, revocation, the mistakes that actually happen

## Platforms

- [Rust](https://dat.saro.me/llms/platform-rust.md): Crate `dat`, cargo features, `DatCmsManager` / `DatManager`, `DatError` matching - the reference implementation
- [Java & Kotlin](https://dat.saro.me/llms/platform-jvm.md): `me.saro:dat`, `DatResult` instead of exceptions, both languages side by side
- [JavaScript & TypeScript](https://dat.saro.me/llms/platform-javascript.md): `saro-dat`, Node 24 + ESM requirements, async API, BigInt time arguments
- [Python](https://dat.saro.me/llms/platform-python.md): `saro-dat`, builder setup, `DatError` catching, FastAPI dependency
- [C#](https://dat.saro.me/llms/platform-csharp.md): `saro-dat`, `IDisposable` lifetimes, DI registration, exception filters
- [Go](https://dat.saro.me/llms/platform-go.md): `github.com/saro-lab/dat/dat-go/v4`, sentinel errors, `dat.Code` / `dat.Retry` helpers
- [Ruby](https://dat.saro.me/llms/platform-ruby.md): `saro-dat`, `Saro::Dat::Error` rescuing, Rack middleware
- [C & C++](https://dat.saro.me/llms/platform-c.md): vcpkg port, out-parameter and ownership conventions, CMS without a builder

## Optional

- [Full docs site](https://dat.saro.me/): The same material written for people, in many languages
- [Source](https://github.com/saro-lab/dat): Every client and the CMS server in one repository
- [DAT CMS](https://dat.saro.me/svc/docker-saro-lab-dat-cms): The certificate management service - Docker, Kubernetes, binary
